source_lines.29: A **finite two-way relay channel** is the three-node DMN of [[def-finite-discrete-memoryless-network-and-code]] with terminal inputs $X_1,X_2$, relay input $X_r$, terminal outputs $Y_1,Y_2$, relay observation $Y_r$, and transition law $W(y_1,y_2,y_r\mid x_1,x_2,x_r)$. Terminals 1 and 2 have independent uniform messages $M_1$ and $M_2$ and wish to exchange them. A causal code uses $X_{1,i}=f_{1,i}(M_1,Y_1^{i-1})$, $X_{2,i}=f_{2,i}(M_2,Y_2^{i-1})$, and $X_{r,i}=f_{r,i}(Y_r^{i-1})$; terminal 1 estimates $M_2$ from $(M_1,Y_1^n)$ and terminal 2 estimates $M_1$ from $(M_2,Y_2^n)$. The probability of error is the probability either estimate is wrong. This is a full-duplex model: all three nodes choose an input at every use, and each input depends only on that node's message and past observations.

source_lines.41: Let $S_1,S_2,\ldots$ be IID with probability vector $P_S$ on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal S$, and let $W$ be a finite DMC with capacity $C(W)$ in nats per channel use. Write $H(P_S):=-\sum_{s:P_S(s)>0}P_S(s)\ln P_S(s)$ for source entropy in nats. Fix positive integers $n_k$ with $n_k/k\to\rho\in(0,\infty)$. A deterministic $(k,n_k)$ joint code is as in [[def-it-point-to-point-joint-source-channel-code]]. If $H(P_S)=0$, a zero-error code sequence exists for every such $W$. If $H(P_S)<\rho C(W)$, there are codes with block error tending to zero. Conversely, every code sequence with block error tending to zero satisfies $H(P_S)\le\rho C(W)$. Thus strict violation $H(P_S)>\rho C(W)$ rules out reliable transmission; the positive-entropy equality boundary is not asserted.
